text.p: A federal judge who postponed a trial in the Whitewater investigation refused Thursday to reconsider his decision or to allow another judge to consider the question.
U.S. District Judge Stephen Reasoner rejected arguments by Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth Starr that he was biased in favour of a witness used by the defence to urge the delay.

Last week Reasoner delayed indefinitely the trial of former Arkansas Gov. Jim Guy Tucker, who Starr has accused of bankruptcy fraud. Reasoner said Tucker's recent liver transplant surgery made a trial inadvisable, and cited a medical report from a doctor who treated both Tucker and Reasoner.
Starr countered that Reasoner's relationship with the doctor lent the appearance of bias and asked that Reasoner allow another judge to consider the medical evidence.

Tucker was scheduled for trial in September. He was convicted last year of fraud and conspiracy in another case brought by Starr, who said he uncovered the offences while investigating the personal and political finances of President and Mrs. Clinton.
Tucker succeeded Clinton as governor of Arkansas.
Two of Clinton's former business partners were convicted with Tucker.
